environment.description: Application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an internal ALB (not internet-facing). Traffic reaches the ALB only through an API Gateway HTTP API integration with a Lambda authorizer. The PostgreSQL 14 RDS instance uses a restricted role connected via RDS Proxy with IAM authentication. The database role (app_search_ro) is configured with a row-level security policy and critically, the pg_hba.conf on the RDS parameter group sets the connection's statement_timeout to 50ms and uses a SECURITY DEFINER function wrapper. The RDS instance has a custom parameter group with: log_min_duration_statement=0, pg_stat_statements enabled, and most importantly pgaudit.log='all' combined with a CloudWatch subscription filter triggering a Lambda that calls rds.modify_db_cluster to force-failover on anomalous query patterns. However, the PRIMARY control is that the RDS custom parameter group sets `session_preload_libraries = 'auto_explain,pg_stat_statements'` and the database role has `ALTER ROLE app_search_ro SET plan_cache_mode = 'force_generic_plan'` combined with `ALTER ROLE app_search_ro SET statement_timeout = '100ms'`. The role also has ONLY `GRANT SELECT (id, name, price, category) ON products TO app_search_ro` — column-level SELECT grant excluding the description column, and NO access to any other table (pg_catalog system tables are accessible but information_schema is revoked via `REVOKE SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA information_schema FROM app_search_ro`).

config.compute: ECS Fargate, internal ALB, API Gateway fronting
config.database_grants: GRANT SELECT (id, name, price, category) ON products TO app_search_ro; REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA information_schema FROM app_search_ro; REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA information_schema FROM app_search_ro;
config.role_settings: ALTER ROLE app_search_ro SET statement_timeout = '100ms'; ALTER ROLE app_search_ro SET plan_cache_mode = 'force_generic_plan';
config.network: RDS in private subnet, accessible only from ECS tasks SG, no public endpoint
config.api_gateway: HTTP API with Lambda authorizer, rate limit 100 req/s per API key
